channel.title: The Wyoming Truth - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Wyoming Truth (wyomingtruth.org)

item.title: Trump and Netanyahu Split on Gas Field Attack, Raise Questions About Whether They’re in Sync on War - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ‘s diverging language on Israel’s decision to attack a critical Iranian gas field marks the most notable difference of opinion between the two leaders since the start of the 20-day war against Iran.

item.title: Democrats Aim to Turn Trump’s Tariffs Against GOP in Campaigns for Governor - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — Less than a week after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump’s global tariffs, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul listened as one of the plaintiffs in the case recounted the financial toll of the levies on his wine importing business.

item.title: Cuba Refuses to Let US Embassy in Havana Import Diesel for its Generators - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Cuban government has refused a request by the U.S. Embassy in Havana to allow it to import diesel for its generators while the Trump administration continues to impose a fuel blockade on the island, two U.S. officials familiar with the matter said Friday.

item.title: Congress Looks for Trump’s Exit Plan as the Iran War Drags On - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump took the United States to war without a vote of support from Congress, but lawmakers are increasingly questioning when, how and at what cost the war with Iran will come to an end.

item.title: Democrats Sharpen Criticism of Vance as They Look Past Trump to the 2028 Presidential Campaign - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: FAIRFIELD, Ohio (AP) — Although President Donald Trump is the top Democratic nemesis, some of the party’s most ambitious leaders are increasingly looking past him and at Vice President JD Vance.

item.title: Trump’s EPA is Paving the Way for Haze to Return to National Parks, Conservationists Warn - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: MADISON, Wis. (AP) — A year ago, federal environmental regulators told West Virginia officials that their plan to clear sulfur and smog from skies over the state’s national wilderness areas wasn’t good enough because a dozen coal plants didn’t analyze whether they needed better pollution controls.

item.title: Trump’s Changing Course on Strait of Hormuz Strategy Raises Questions About US War Preparation - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WEST PALM BEACH, Fla. (AP) — At war with Iran, President Donald Trump is cycling through an increasingly desperate list of options as he searches for a solution to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. He has jumped from calls to secure the waterway through diplomatic means to lifting sanctions and now escalating to a direct threat against civilian infrastructure in the Islamic Republic.

item.title: ICE Officers will Begin Assisting TSA as Shutdown Frustrates Travelers and Screeners - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump’s decision to order federal immigration agents to U.S. airports to help with security during a budget impasse is drawing concerns that their presence may escalate tensions among air travelers frustrated over hourslong waits and screeners angry about missed paychecks.

item.title: It’s a Bad Time to Hunt for New Jobs, Most US Workers Say in New Gallup Poll - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: WASHINGTON (AP) — Americans’ outlook on the job market has turned increasingly pessimistic, a surprisingly negative shift given the low unemployment rate but one that likely reflects an ongoing hiring drought.

item.title: Abortion Pills are Gaining Ground as a Method for Ending Pregnancies, and Opponents are Responding - The Wyoming Truth
item.description: As states that already ban abortion look to further restrict access this year, much of the focus is on pills sent by out-of-state providers.
